title: Reduce research-source validation peak allocation by 42% (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Reduce complete research-source metadata validation's peak traced allocation by about 42% on a real large-source package. This is a verifier-engineering contribution with a scoped equivalence proof and finite tests. No new κ is claimed.

```diff
 source blob ID and SHA256 checks
-compare pinned bytes with a second whole-file allocation
+compare every working-file byte through a reusable buffer of at most 1 MiB
 retain source-drift rejection and cleanup
```

The production change adds one helper and replaces one comparison. The existing stable regular-file checkout contract remains required. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

## Evidence

Five alternating fresh-process pairs run complete, unchanged `validate` calls on `research/physical-gaussian-core`, including its 54,548,480-byte archive input. All ten complete task/manifest results match and no validation fails. The package's scientific verifier is not run or audited.

- Peak traced Python allocation: baseline 127,510,623 bytes in every pair; candidate median 74,011,826 bytes, range 74,011,708–74,011,826.
- Traced validation time has a cost: baseline median 0.232871 s, range 0.225368–0.253928; candidate median 0.330213 s, range 0.329083–0.340037. No runtime speedup is claimed.
- CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, warm OS caches. The generated `BENCHMARK.json` retains raw samples, environment, source hashes and complete-output hashes. These measure Python traced allocation, not RSS or whole scientific replay.
- Seven normal/optimized contract tests cover equal binary/chunk-boundary files, same-size drift, truncation/append, open errors, late read failure after an earlier mismatch, closure, restored inputs and unchanged blob/SHA rejection.
- Both registered commands pass locally; direct normal/optimized checks took 0.60 s and 0.68 s against 30-second limits. Committed bytes/source ancestry and all three export input declarations pass at `ac7949b52fb71417bc5d48b8a562042b8e78cf89`. Read-only exported normal/optimized replays pass, with all 12 exported files unchanged.
- The complete tooling suite runs 685 tests: 654 pass, 29 skip on this host, and only the two unchanged main-baseline documentation tests below fail. Command: `/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py' -v`.

From the repository root, set `TMPDIR` to an external scratch directory and run:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/source-comparison-memory/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/source-comparison-memory/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/source-comparison-memory
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/source-comparison-memory --check-source-history
```

For the optional benchmark, materialize `research/physical-gaussian-core` and `references/semantic-bulk/rad20` first in a sparse checkout, then run:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/source-comparison-memory/benchmark.py --work /absolute/new/scratch --pairs 5
```

Elsewhere substitute a local CPython 3.12 interpreter. Git is needed for source metadata and the temporary test fixtures. The benchmark baseline is main `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`.

## Limitations

The pinned Git blob is still allocated in full. The 1 MiB bound covers the comparison's additional data buffer. Concurrent mutation is outside the existing checkout-stability contract. Native Windows execution, whole-process RSS and scientific/full selected replays remain unrun; mathematical, physical and supplier obligations are unchanged. The complete validator is slower in these traced measurements.

## Open next questions

Can the retained pinned Git blob also be streamed while preserving blob identity, SHA256, response framing, final process status and cleanup? First specify a bounded chunk protocol and all existing consumers; the present complete-bytes `git_blobs` interface blocks that next step.

## Related open work

- #6162 reuses already authenticated committed metadata in publication byte/history checks; this PR bounds a working-file comparison buffer in registered-package validation. The commands, fixtures and measured quantities differ, and no combined performance is claimed.
- #6155 removes mismatch-only diagnostic hashing from publication byte/history checks on the same Gaussian fixture; it changes a different command. No combined performance is measured.
- #6087 reuses planner input-path validation within an invocation; this changes live source-byte comparison during full package validation.
- #5721 integrates Windows Job Object ownership in the Git blob reader; the reader and its ownership/cleanup implementation are unchanged here.
- #6050 repairs selected-replay CI navigation; this PR retains that separate documentation issue.

Credit Douglas Colkitt's runner; woklerx/PR1452, Arham-Tahir64/PR1595 and ywz65/PR2539 for the source-reader lineage; later path, deadline, replacement-ref and descendant-cleanup contributors; and Jose Manuel/jmbarrancoml for the unchanged benchmark package. Buffered I/O and memory views are standard methods.

## CI notes

**Uncertified by CI** at head `ac7949b52fb71417bc5d48b8a562042b8e78cf89`. In [run 40725920133](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40725920133), `plan` fails and `replay (research/source-comparison-memory)` is skipped. **The package replay did not run in CI.** A maintainer re-run is needed after main is fixed.

The only two failures are inherited onboarding documentation mismatches on canonical main `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`, the PR6030 admission committed with `[skip ci]`. That commit changed the selected record without matching the status and CI navigation pages:

- `test_research_current_status.CurrentStatusTests.test_current_section_matches_selected_record` expects standalone `**0.003125804**` in `docs/research/current-status.md`; the page bolds the larger expression `0.003125804 = 781451/250000000`.
- `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record` expects `make frontier6030-verify`; the CI navigation page, read from `docs/ci-verification.md` by the test, still names #5599 and `make frontier5599-verify`.

The hosted run reports `Ran 685 tests` and `FAILED (failures=2, skipped=23)`. These are the same two failures seen locally and in PR #6120's [run 40691776027](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40691776027). Open PR #6050 targets the documentation fix. Neither failing document nor the selected record is changed here.

Local normal/optimized package replay, committed-byte/source-history checks and read-only export replays remain separate evidence. No hosted package certification is claimed. Shared-runner changes select every registered package in the existing planner; no historical scientific suites were launched locally.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

**Blast Radius:** Validation

All registered package source checks use this comparison. The written proof and behavioral controls preserve exact acceptance under the existing checkout contract; the measured memory/time tradeoff is explicit.
